# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1558._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_trajectory.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa trajectory tail` goes permanently silent for any session larger than the window residency**

The count-based `TrajectoryTailer` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:120-128`) dedupes by list length:

```dart
List<String> tail(List<SessionRecord> records) {
  if (records.length <= _seen) return const [];
  final fresh = records.sublist(_seen);
  _seen = records.length;
  ...
}
```

Composed with this PR's two changes, the headless `tail` verb deadlocks itself:

1. Line 40 (`await session.ensureWholeLedgerResident();`) runs for **every** verb, including `tail`. The initial `tailer.tail(records)` therefore sees the WHOLE ledger (N records — the PR's own `session_tree_test` proves 800 records page in), so `_seen = N`.
2. Each poll re-opens a **fresh windowed** session and calls `getBranch()` — which returns only the ~200-record resident tail window (the rework summary itself notes "200 resident at open").
3. `fresh.length` (~200) `<= _seen` (N) → `tail()` returns `const []` on **every poll, forever**. No error, no exit code change — the command just stops emitting.

This breaks `fa trajectory tail` not only for the incident-class giant sessions but for **any session with more than ~200 records**, which is exactly the population this PR targets. CI stays green because no test exercises the headless tail against a >window session (the `/trajectory tail` test in `trajectory_cli_test.dart` rides the live-session path in `trajectory_commands.dart`, which is a different code path and unaffected).

**Fix options** (either works):

- Poll the *original* `session` object instead of re-opening: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and its live-tail ingest (`_ingestAtTail`, `windowed_session_storage.dart:736`) picks up the appended suffix on each `getBranch()`, so the branch list genuinely grows past `_seen`.
- Or skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` for the `tail` verb entirely (the tailer never needs the head) — cheaper startup, though the initial print then covers only the resident window instead of the old full-branch parity; if that parity matters, pair it with option 1.

A regression test should seed >window records (e.g. 300), tail headlessly, append, and assert the new record renders — see `comment4` below.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (called unconditionally from `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:40` for `view`/`cost`/`inspect`) therefore degrades "clean refusal with remediation guidance" into "long hang, then probable VM crash" for exactly the sessions this ticket is about. These surfaces genuinely need the whole ledger today, so this is not a blocker — but until AC3a streaming lands, please add a cheap pre-check (`await _reader.stat()` size vs. a bound, e.g. the same 2 GiB) that throws the same `tooLarge` `SessionException` with the repair hint before the scan starts. That keeps the honest degradation contract (F3 NEG) for the truly-giant case while the chunked scan fixes the merely-large one.

Two smaller notes on the same method:

- If the scan loop breaks early on `chunk.isEmpty` (file truncated below `top` mid-scan), `_hasOlder` is still set to `false` and the window claims full residency over a range that was never read. It follows the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention, so consistent — but worth a comment that an early empty read here means *truncation*, not *clean EOF at the head*.
- `_spliceOlderAbove` is byte-for-byte the same splice logic as the new `prepend` block in `_indexChunk` (three `insertAll` + the identical per-record index/`_appendedBelow.remove`/label-cache loop). Extract one shared `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` so the next window-layout change can't update one copy and miss the other.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the block-prepend splice now living in `_indexChunk`**

The body here (three `insertAll(0, …)` calls plus the per-record `_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache` loop) is identical to the new `prepend` branch of `_indexChunk` at `windowed_session_storage.dart:937-958`. Both were introduced in this PR. Extract a single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` and call it from both sites — the window-list invariant (three parallel lists kept in the same file order) is exactly the kind of thing that drifts when two copies exist.

---

### Thread 4 — `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: add a headless `tail` regression test with more records than the residency window**

This test group proves windowed resolution and whole-ledger materialization, but nothing exercises the `tail` verb's poll loop against a session bigger than the ~200-record window residency — which is why the poll-window/`TrajectoryTailer._seen` interaction in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` (see the BLOCKING finding) ships green. A cheap version: seed ~300 records, run the headless tail verb in a zone/fake clock or factor the poll loop, append one record, and assert a new row renders. Even a pure composition test (`TrajectoryTailer` fed by a fresh windowed open's `getBranch()` after a whole-ledger prime) would have caught the silent-stall.

---

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The windowed-everywhere migration is well-executed (block-prepend `_indexChunk`, sequential `loadAllOlder`, foreign-repo degradation, incident-shape fixtures), but one BLOCKING regression: the headless `fa trajectory tail` poll re-opens windowed while the tailer dedupes by count after a whole-ledger prime — so tail goes permanently silent for any session larger than the ~200-record residency window (the exact class this PR targets). One IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` materializes the whole ledger with no size guard, trading the gh-1073 clean refusal for a long-then-OOM failure mode. Verified locally: `dart analyze` clean on touched files; 32 + 50 targeted tests pass.

**Key Issues**:
1. 🚨 `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:103` — tail poll returns `const []` forever once `_seen` (whole-ledger count) exceeds the windowed branch length
2. ⚠️ `windowed_session_storage.dart:429` — `loadAllOlder` has no pre-scan size bound; giant ledgers OOM instead of failing fast with `tooLarge` + repair hint
3. 💡 `windowed_session_storage.dart:497` — `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the `_indexChunk` prepend splice
4. 💡 Test gap: no headless tail test over a >window session

**Next Steps**:
1. Poll the original `session` object (live-tail ingest) or skip the whole-ledger prime for `tail`
2. Add a `stat()`-based size pre-check in `loadAllOlder` throwing the existing `tooLarge` `SessionException` until AC3a streaming lands
3. Extract a shared `_blockPrepend`; add the tail regression test

---

# pr-1558: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable ## Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:22:30Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.

blocks.text:
# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1558._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_trajectory.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa trajectory tail` goes permanently silent for any session larger than the window residency**

The count-based `TrajectoryTailer` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:120-128`) dedupes by list length:

```dart
List<String> tail(List<SessionRecord> records) {
  if (records.length <= _seen) return const [];
  final fresh = records.sublist(_seen);
  _seen = records.length;
  ...
}
```

Composed with this PR's two changes, the headless `tail` verb deadlocks itself:

1. Line 40 (`await session.ensureWholeLedgerResident();`) runs for **every** verb, including `tail`. The initial `tailer.tail(records)` therefore sees the WHOLE ledger (N records — the PR's own `session_tree_test` proves 800 records page in), so `_seen = N`.
2. Each poll re-opens a **fresh windowed** session and calls `getBranch()` — which returns only the ~200-record resident tail window (the rework summary itself notes "200 resident at open").
3. `fresh.length` (~200) `<= _seen` (N) → `tail()` returns `const []` on **every poll, forever**. No error, no exit code change — the command just stops emitting.

This breaks `fa trajectory tail` not only for the incident-class giant sessions but for **any session with more than ~200 records**, which is exactly the population this PR targets. CI stays green because no test exercises the headless tail against a >window session (the `/trajectory tail` test in `trajectory_cli_test.dart` rides the live-session path in `trajectory_commands.dart`, which is a different code path and unaffected).

**Fix options** (either works):

- Poll the *original* `session` object instead of re-opening: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and its live-tail ingest (`_ingestAtTail`, `windowed_session_storage.dart:736`) picks up the appended suffix on each `getBranch()`, so the branch list genuinely grows past `_seen`.
- Or skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` for the `tail` verb entirely (the tailer never needs the head) — cheaper startup, though the initial print then covers only the resident window instead of the old full-branch parity; if that parity matters, pair it with option 1.

A regression test should seed >window records (e.g. 300), tail headlessly, append, and assert the new record renders — see `comment4` below.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (called unconditionally from `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:40` for `view`/`cost`/`inspect`) therefore degrades "clean refusal with remediation guidance" into "long hang, then probable VM crash" for exactly the sessions this ticket is about. These surfaces genuinely need the whole ledger today, so this is not a blocker — but until AC3a streaming lands, please add a cheap pre-check (`await _reader.stat()` size vs. a bound, e.g. the same 2 GiB) that throws the same `tooLarge` `SessionException` with the repair hint before the scan starts. That keeps the honest degradation contract (F3 NEG) for the truly-giant case while the chunked scan fixes the merely-large one.

Two smaller notes on the same method:

- If the scan loop breaks early on `chunk.isEmpty` (file truncated below `top` mid-scan), `_hasOlder` is still set to `false` and the window claims full residency over a range that was never read. It follows the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention, so consistent — but worth a comment that an early empty read here means *truncation*, not *clean EOF at the head*.
- `_spliceOlderAbove` is byte-for-byte the same splice logic as the new `prepend` block in `_indexChunk` (three `insertAll` + the identical per-record index/`_appendedBelow.remove`/label-cache loop). Extract one shared `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` so the next window-layout change can't update one copy and miss the other.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the block-prepend splice now living in `_indexChunk`**

The body here (three `insertAll(0, …)` calls plus the per-record `_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache` loop) is identical to the new `prepend` branch of `_indexChunk` at `windowed_session_storage.dart:937-958`. Both were introduced in this PR. Extract a single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` and call it from both sites — the window-list invariant (three parallel lists kept in the same file order) is exactly the kind of thing that drifts when two copies exist.

---

# pr-1558: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable ## Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before [before W1] P1[Picker / resume / trajectory / child preview] --> F[repo.open full] F -->|> 2 GiB| X[SessionException tooLarge] end subgraph after [after W1] P2[Picker · /resume · name scan · child preview] --> W[repo.open windowed] T[fa trajectory view/cost/inspect] --> W W --> H[ensureWholeLedgerResident
loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1558._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_trajectory.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa trajectory tail` goes permanently silent for any session larger than the window residency**

The count-based `TrajectoryTailer` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:120-128`) dedupes by list length:

```dart
List<String> tail(List<SessionRecord> records) {
  if (records.length <= _seen) return const [];
  final fresh = records.sublist(_seen);
  _seen = records.length;
  ...
}
```

Composed with this PR's two changes, the headless `tail` verb deadlocks itself:

1. Line 40 (`await session.ensureWholeLedgerResident();`) runs for **every** verb, including `tail`. The initial `tailer.tail(records)` therefore sees the WHOLE ledger (N records — the PR's own `session_tree_test` proves 800 records page in), so `_seen = N`.
2. Each poll re-opens a **fresh windowed** session and calls `getBranch()` — which returns only the ~200-record resident tail window (the rework summary itself notes "200 resident at open").
3. `fresh.length` (~200) `<= _seen` (N) → `tail()` returns `const []` on **every poll, forever**. No error, no exit code change — the command just stops emitting.

This breaks `fa trajectory tail` not only for the incident-class giant sessions but for **any session with more than ~200 records**, which is exactly the population this PR targets. CI stays green because no test exercises the headless tail against a >window session (the `/trajectory tail` test in `trajectory_cli_test.dart` rides the live-session path in `trajectory_commands.dart`, which is a different code path and unaffected).

**Fix options** (either works):

- Poll the *original* `session` object instead of re-opening: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and its live-tail ingest (`_ingestAtTail`, `windowed_session_storage.dart:736`) picks up the appended suffix on each `getBranch()`, so the branch list genuinely grows past `_seen`.
- Or skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` for the `tail` verb entirely (the tailer never needs the head) — cheaper startup, though the initial print then covers only the resident window instead of the old full-branch parity; if that parity matters, pair it with option 1.

A regression test should seed >window records (e.g. 300), tail headlessly, append, and assert the new record renders — see `comment4` below.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (called unconditionally from `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:40` for `view`/`cost`/`inspect`) therefore degrades "clean refusal with remediation guidance" into "long hang, then probable VM crash" for exactly the sessions this ticket is about. These surfaces genuinely need the whole ledger today, so this is not a blocker — but until AC3a streaming lands, please add a cheap pre-check (`await _reader.stat()` size vs. a bound, e.g. the same 2 GiB) that throws the same `tooLarge` `SessionException` with the repair hint before the scan starts. That keeps the honest degradation contract (F3 NEG) for the truly-giant case while the chunked scan fixes the merely-large one.

Two smaller notes on the same method:

- If the scan loop breaks early on `chunk.isEmpty` (file truncated below `top` mid-scan), `_hasOlder` is still set to `false` and the window claims full residency over a range that was never read. It follows the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention, so consistent — but worth a comment that an early empty read here means *truncation*, not *clean EOF at the head*.
- `_spliceOlderAbove` is byte-for-byte the same splice logic as the new `prepend` block in `_indexChunk` (three `insertAll` + the identical per-record index/`_appendedBelow.remove`/label-cache loop). Extract one shared `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` so the next window-layout change can't update one copy and miss the other.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the block-prepend splice now living in `_indexChunk`**

The body here (three `insertAll(0, …)` calls plus the per-record `_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache` loop) is identical to the new `prepend` branch of `_indexChunk` at `windowed_session_storage.dart:937-958`. Both were introduced in this PR. Extract a single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` and call it from both sites — the window-list invariant (three parallel lists kept in the same file order) is exactly the kind of thing that drifts when two copies exist.

---

### Thread 4 — `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: add a headless `tail` regression test with more records than the residency window**

This test group proves windowed resolution and whole-ledger materialization, but nothing exercises the `tail` verb's poll loop against a session bigger than the ~200-record window residency — which is why the poll-window/`TrajectoryTailer._seen` interaction in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` (see the BLOCKING finding) ships green. A cheap version: seed ~300 records, run the headless tail verb in a zone/fake clock or factor the poll loop, append one record, and assert a new row renders. Even a pure composition test (`TrajectoryTailer` fed by a fresh windowed open's `getBranch()` after a whole-ledger prime) would have caught the silent-stall.

---

**Summary**: The windowed-everywhere migration is well-executed (block-prepend `_indexChunk`, sequential `loadAllOlder`, foreign-repo degradation, incident-shape fixtures), but one BLOCKING regression: the headless `fa trajectory tail` poll re-opens windowed while the tailer dedupes by count after a whole-ledger prime — so tail goes permanently silent for any session larger than the ~200-record residency window (the exact class this PR targets). # pr-1558: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable ## Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.

loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1558._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_trajectory.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa trajectory tail` goes permanently silent for any session larger than the window residency**

The count-based `TrajectoryTailer` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:120-128`) dedupes by list length:

```dart
List<String> tail(List<SessionRecord> records) {
  if (records.length <= _seen) return const [];
  final fresh = records.sublist(_seen);
  _seen = records.length;
  ...
}
```

Composed with this PR's two changes, the headless `tail` verb deadlocks itself:

1. Line 40 (`await session.ensureWholeLedgerResident();`) runs for **every** verb, including `tail`. The initial `tailer.tail(records)` therefore sees the WHOLE ledger (N records — the PR's own `session_tree_test` proves 800 records page in), so `_seen = N`.
2. Each poll re-opens a **fresh windowed** session and calls `getBranch()` — which returns only the ~200-record resident tail window (the rework summary itself notes "200 resident at open").
3. `fresh.length` (~200) `<= _seen` (N) → `tail()` returns `const []` on **every poll, forever**. No error, no exit code change — the command just stops emitting.

This breaks `fa trajectory tail` not only for the incident-class giant sessions but for **any session with more than ~200 records**, which is exactly the population this PR targets. CI stays green because no test exercises the headless tail against a >window session (the `/trajectory tail` test in `trajectory_cli_test.dart` rides the live-session path in `trajectory_commands.dart`, which is a different code path and unaffected).

**Fix options** (either works):

- Poll the *original* `session` object instead of re-opening: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and its live-tail ingest (`_ingestAtTail`, `windowed_session_storage.dart:736`) picks up the appended suffix on each `getBranch()`, so the branch list genuinely grows past `_seen`.
- Or skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` for the `tail` verb entirely (the tailer never needs the head) — cheaper startup, though the initial print then covers only the resident window instead of the old full-branch parity; if that parity matters, pair it with option 1.

A regression test should seed >window records (e.g. 300), tail headlessly, append, and assert the new record renders — see `comment4` below.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (called unconditionally from `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:40` for `view`/`cost`/`inspect`) therefore degrades "clean refusal with remediation guidance" into "long hang, then probable VM crash" for exactly the sessions this ticket is about. These surfaces genuinely need the whole ledger today, so this is not a blocker — but until AC3a streaming lands, please add a cheap pre-check (`await _reader.stat()` size vs. a bound, e.g. the same 2 GiB) that throws the same `tooLarge` `SessionException` with the repair hint before the scan starts. That keeps the honest degradation contract (F3 NEG) for the truly-giant case while the chunked scan fixes the merely-large one.

Two smaller notes on the same method:

- If the scan loop breaks early on `chunk.isEmpty` (file truncated below `top` mid-scan), `_hasOlder` is still set to `false` and the window claims full residency over a range that was never read. It follows the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention, so consistent — but worth a comment that an early empty read here means *truncation*, not *clean EOF at the head*.
- `_spliceOlderAbove` is byte-for-byte the same splice logic as the new `prepend` block in `_indexChunk` (three `insertAll` + the identical per-record index/`_appendedBelow.remove`/label-cache loop). Extract one shared `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` so the next window-layout change can't update one copy and miss the other.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the block-prepend splice now living in `_indexChunk`**

The body here (three `insertAll(0, …)` calls plus the per-record `_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache` loop) is identical to the new `prepend` branch of `_indexChunk` at `windowed_session_storage.dart:937-958`. Both were introduced in this PR. Extract a single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` and call it from both sites — the window-list invariant (three parallel lists kept in the same file order) is exactly the kind of thing that drifts when two copies exist.

---

### Thread 4 — `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: add a headless `tail` regression test with more records than the residency window**

This test group proves windowed resolution and whole-ledger materialization, but nothing exercises the `tail` verb's poll loop against a session bigger than the ~200-record window residency — which is why the poll-window/`TrajectoryTailer._seen` interaction in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` (see the BLOCKING finding) ships green. A cheap version: seed ~300 records, run the headless tail verb in a zone/fake clock or factor the poll loop, append one record, and assert a new row renders. Even a pure composition test (`TrajectoryTailer` fed by a fresh windowed open's `getBranch()` after a whole-ledger prime) would have caught the silent-stall.

---

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The windowed-everywhere migration is well-executed (block-prepend `_indexChunk`, sequential `loadAllOlder`, foreign-repo degradation, incident-shape fixtures), but one BLOCKING regression: the headless `fa trajectory tail` poll re-opens windowed while the tailer dedupes by count after a whole-ledger prime — so tail goes permanently silent for any session larger than the ~200-record residency window (the exact class this PR targets). # pr-1558: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable ## Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.

paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). blocks.text:
# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1558._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_trajectory.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa trajectory tail` goes permanently silent for any session larger than the window residency**

The count-based `TrajectoryTailer` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:120-128`) dedupes by list length:

```dart
List<String> tail(List<SessionRecord> records) {
  if (records.length <= _seen) return const [];
  final fresh = records.sublist(_seen);
  _seen = records.length;
  ...
}
```

Composed with this PR's two changes, the headless `tail` verb deadlocks itself:

1. Line 40 (`await session.ensureWholeLedgerResident();`) runs for **every** verb, including `tail`. The initial `tailer.tail(records)` therefore sees the WHOLE ledger (N records — the PR's own `session_tree_test` proves 800 records page in), so `_seen = N`.
2. Each poll re-opens a **fresh windowed** session and calls `getBranch()` — which returns only the ~200-record resident tail window (the rework summary itself notes "200 resident at open").
3. `fresh.length` (~200) `<= _seen` (N) → `tail()` returns `const []` on **every poll, forever**. No error, no exit code change — the command just stops emitting.

This breaks `fa trajectory tail` not only for the incident-class giant sessions but for **any session with more than ~200 records**, which is exactly the population this PR targets. CI stays green because no test exercises the headless tail against a >window session (the `/trajectory tail` test in `trajectory_cli_test.dart` rides the live-session path in `trajectory_commands.dart`, which is a different code path and unaffected).

**Fix options** (either works):

- Poll the *original* `session` object instead of re-opening: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and its live-tail ingest (`_ingestAtTail`, `windowed_session_storage.dart:736`) picks up the appended suffix on each `getBranch()`, so the branch list genuinely grows past `_seen`.
- Or skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` for the `tail` verb entirely (the tailer never needs the head) — cheaper startup, though the initial print then covers only the resident window instead of the old full-branch parity; if that parity matters, pair it with option 1.

A regression test should seed >window records (e.g. 300), tail headlessly, append, and assert the new record renders — see `comment4` below.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (called unconditionally from `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:40` for `view`/`cost`/`inspect`) therefore degrades "clean refusal with remediation guidance" into "long hang, then probable VM crash" for exactly the sessions this ticket is about. These surfaces genuinely need the whole ledger today, so this is not a blocker — but until AC3a streaming lands, please add a cheap pre-check (`await _reader.stat()` size vs. a bound, e.g. the same 2 GiB) that throws the same `tooLarge` `SessionException` with the repair hint before the scan starts. That keeps the honest degradation contract (F3 NEG) for the truly-giant case while the chunked scan fixes the merely-large one.

Two smaller notes on the same method:

- If the scan loop breaks early on `chunk.isEmpty` (file truncated below `top` mid-scan), `_hasOlder` is still set to `false` and the window claims full residency over a range that was never read. It follows the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention, so consistent — but worth a comment that an early empty read here means *truncation*, not *clean EOF at the head*.
- `_spliceOlderAbove` is byte-for-byte the same splice logic as the new `prepend` block in `_indexChunk` (three `insertAll` + the identical per-record index/`_appendedBelow.remove`/label-cache loop). Extract one shared `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` so the next window-layout change can't update one copy and miss the other.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the block-prepend splice now living in `_indexChunk`**

The body here (three `insertAll(0, …)` calls plus the per-record `_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache` loop) is identical to the new `prepend` branch of `_indexChunk` at `windowed_session_storage.dart:937-958`. Both were introduced in this PR. Extract a single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` and call it from both sites — the window-list invariant (three parallel lists kept in the same file order) is exactly the kind of thing that drifts when two copies exist.

---

### Thread 4 — `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: add a headless `tail` regression test with more records than the residency window**

This test group proves windowed resolution and whole-ledger materialization, but nothing exercises the `tail` verb's poll loop against a session bigger than the ~200-record window residency — which is why the poll-window/`TrajectoryTailer._seen` interaction in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` (see the BLOCKING finding) ships green. A cheap version: seed ~300 records, run the headless tail verb in a zone/fake clock or factor the poll loop, append one record, and assert a new row renders. Even a pure composition test (`TrajectoryTailer` fed by a fresh windowed open's `getBranch()` after a whole-ledger prime) would have caught the silent-stall.

---

# pr-1558: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable ## Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.

loadAllOlder: bounded blocks, one splice] W --> N[resolveSessionName
paged name lookup] TL[fa trajectory tail] --> W end ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1558 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1558 - **Title**: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1555` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 11 - **Additions**: +586 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-11T21:05:18Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:22:30Z ## PR Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1558._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_trajectory.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa trajectory tail` goes permanently silent for any session larger than the window residency**

The count-based `TrajectoryTailer` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:120-128`) dedupes by list length:

```dart
List<String> tail(List<SessionRecord> records) {
  if (records.length <= _seen) return const [];
  final fresh = records.sublist(_seen);
  _seen = records.length;
  ...
}
```

Composed with this PR's two changes, the headless `tail` verb deadlocks itself:

1. Line 40 (`await session.ensureWholeLedgerResident();`) runs for **every** verb, including `tail`. The initial `tailer.tail(records)` therefore sees the WHOLE ledger (N records — the PR's own `session_tree_test` proves 800 records page in), so `_seen = N`.
2. Each poll re-opens a **fresh windowed** session and calls `getBranch()` — which returns only the ~200-record resident tail window (the rework summary itself notes "200 resident at open").
3. `fresh.length` (~200) `<= _seen` (N) → `tail()` returns `const []` on **every poll, forever**. No error, no exit code change — the command just stops emitting.

This breaks `fa trajectory tail` not only for the incident-class giant sessions but for **any session with more than ~200 records**, which is exactly the population this PR targets. CI stays green because no test exercises the headless tail against a >window session (the `/trajectory tail` test in `trajectory_cli_test.dart` rides the live-session path in `trajectory_commands.dart`, which is a different code path and unaffected).

**Fix options** (either works):

- Poll the *original* `session` object instead of re-opening: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and its live-tail ingest (`_ingestAtTail`, `windowed_session_storage.dart:736`) picks up the appended suffix on each `getBranch()`, so the branch list genuinely grows past `_seen`.
- Or skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` for the `tail` verb entirely (the tailer never needs the head) — cheaper startup, though the initial print then covers only the resident window instead of the old full-branch parity; if that parity matters, pair it with option 1.

A regression test should seed >window records (e.g. 300), tail headlessly, append, and assert the new record renders — see `comment4` below.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (called unconditionally from `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:40` for `view`/`cost`/`inspect`) therefore degrades "clean refusal with remediation guidance" into "long hang, then probable VM crash" for exactly the sessions this ticket is about. These surfaces genuinely need the whole ledger today, so this is not a blocker — but until AC3a streaming lands, please add a cheap pre-check (`await _reader.stat()` size vs. a bound, e.g. the same 2 GiB) that throws the same `tooLarge` `SessionException` with the repair hint before the scan starts. That keeps the honest degradation contract (F3 NEG) for the truly-giant case while the chunked scan fixes the merely-large one.

Two smaller notes on the same method:

- If the scan loop breaks early on `chunk.isEmpty` (file truncated below `top` mid-scan), `_hasOlder` is still set to `false` and the window claims full residency over a range that was never read. It follows the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention, so consistent — but worth a comment that an early empty read here means *truncation*, not *clean EOF at the head*.
- `_spliceOlderAbove` is byte-for-byte the same splice logic as the new `prepend` block in `_indexChunk` (three `insertAll` + the identical per-record index/`_appendedBelow.remove`/label-cache loop). Extract one shared `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` so the next window-layout change can't update one copy and miss the other.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the block-prepend splice now living in `_indexChunk`**

The body here (three `insertAll(0, …)` calls plus the per-record `_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache` loop) is identical to the new `prepend` branch of `_indexChunk` at `windowed_session_storage.dart:937-958`. Both were introduced in this PR. Extract a single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` and call it from both sites — the window-list invariant (three parallel lists kept in the same file order) is exactly the kind of thing that drifts when two copies exist.

---

### Thread 4 — `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: add a headless `tail` regression test with more records than the residency window**

This test group proves windowed resolution and whole-ledger materialization, but nothing exercises the `tail` verb's poll loop against a session bigger than the ~200-record window residency — which is why the poll-window/`TrajectoryTailer._seen` interaction in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` (see the BLOCKING finding) ships green. A cheap version: seed ~300 records, run the headless tail verb in a zone/fake clock or factor the poll loop, append one record, and assert a new row renders. Even a pure composition test (`TrajectoryTailer` fed by a fresh windowed open's `getBranch()` after a whole-ledger prime) would have caught the silent-stall.

---

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The windowed-everywhere migration is well-executed (block-prepend `_indexChunk`, sequential `loadAllOlder`, foreign-repo degradation, incident-shape fixtures), but one BLOCKING regression: the headless `fa trajectory tail` poll re-opens windowed while the tailer dedupes by count after a whole-ledger prime — so tail goes permanently silent for any session larger than the ~200-record residency window (the exact class this PR targets). # pr-1558: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable ## Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1558._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_trajectory.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa trajectory tail` goes permanently silent for any session larger than the window residency**

The count-based `TrajectoryTailer` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:120-128`) dedupes by list length:

```dart
List<String> tail(List<SessionRecord> records) {
  if (records.length <= _seen) return const [];
  final fresh = records.sublist(_seen);
  _seen = records.length;
  ...
}
```

Composed with this PR's two changes, the headless `tail` verb deadlocks itself:

1. Line 40 (`await session.ensureWholeLedgerResident();`) runs for **every** verb, including `tail`. The initial `tailer.tail(records)` therefore sees the WHOLE ledger (N records — the PR's own `session_tree_test` proves 800 records page in), so `_seen = N`.
2. Each poll re-opens a **fresh windowed** session and calls `getBranch()` — which returns only the ~200-record resident tail window (the rework summary itself notes "200 resident at open").
3. `fresh.length` (~200) `<= _seen` (N) → `tail()` returns `const []` on **every poll, forever**. No error, no exit code change — the command just stops emitting.

This breaks `fa trajectory tail` not only for the incident-class giant sessions but for **any session with more than ~200 records**, which is exactly the population this PR targets. CI stays green because no test exercises the headless tail against a >window session (the `/trajectory tail` test in `trajectory_cli_test.dart` rides the live-session path in `trajectory_commands.dart`, which is a different code path and unaffected).

**Fix options** (either works):

- Poll the *original* `session` object instead of re-opening: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and its live-tail ingest (`_ingestAtTail`, `windowed_session_storage.dart:736`) picks up the appended suffix on each `getBranch()`, so the branch list genuinely grows past `_seen`.
- Or skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` for the `tail` verb entirely (the tailer never needs the head) — cheaper startup, though the initial print then covers only the resident window instead of the old full-branch parity; if that parity matters, pair it with option 1.

A regression test should seed >window records (e.g. 300), tail headlessly, append, and assert the new record renders — see `comment4` below.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (called unconditionally from `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:40` for `view`/`cost`/`inspect`) therefore degrades "clean refusal with remediation guidance" into "long hang, then probable VM crash" for exactly the sessions this ticket is about. These surfaces genuinely need the whole ledger today, so this is not a blocker — but until AC3a streaming lands, please add a cheap pre-check (`await _reader.stat()` size vs. a bound, e.g. the same 2 GiB) that throws the same `tooLarge` `SessionException` with the repair hint before the scan starts. That keeps the honest degradation contract (F3 NEG) for the truly-giant case while the chunked scan fixes the merely-large one.

Two smaller notes on the same method:

- If the scan loop breaks early on `chunk.isEmpty` (file truncated below `top` mid-scan), `_hasOlder` is still set to `false` and the window claims full residency over a range that was never read. It follows the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention, so consistent — but worth a comment that an early empty read here means *truncation*, not *clean EOF at the head*.
- `_spliceOlderAbove` is byte-for-byte the same splice logic as the new `prepend` block in `_indexChunk` (three `insertAll` + the identical per-record index/`_appendedBelow.remove`/label-cache loop). Extract one shared `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` so the next window-layout change can't update one copy and miss the other.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the block-prepend splice now living in `_indexChunk`**

The body here (three `insertAll(0, …)` calls plus the per-record `_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache` loop) is identical to the new `prepend` branch of `_indexChunk` at `windowed_session_storage.dart:937-958`. Both were introduced in this PR. Extract a single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` and call it from both sites — the window-list invariant (three parallel lists kept in the same file order) is exactly the kind of thing that drifts when two copies exist.

---

### Thread 4 — `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):
💡 **SUGGESTION: add a headless `tail` regression test with more records than the residency window**

This test group proves windowed resolution and whole-ledger materialization, but nothing exercises the `tail` verb's poll loop against a session bigger than the ~200-record window residency — which is why the poll-window/`TrajectoryTailer._seen` interaction in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` (see the BLOCKING finding) ships green. A cheap version: seed ~300 records, run the headless tail verb in a zone/fake clock or factor the poll loop, append one record, and assert a new row renders. Even a pure composition test (`TrajectoryTailer` fed by a fresh windowed open's `getBranch()` after a whole-ledger prime) would have caught the silent-stall.

---

# pr-1558: gh-1555 [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable ## Description Closes #1555 ## gh-1555 W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (first shippable slice) ### What changed Migrated the legacy full-open call sites (ticket mechanism d1–d7) to windowed opens so a session past the 2 GiB gh-1073 backstop stays openable on every user-facing read path. The TUI picker (the incident's exact failure path), `/resume`, boot name-resolution, subagent transcript preview, and the headless `fa trajectory` resolver now open windowed; name lookups page via `resolveSessionName()`. The `_loadSession` marathon fallback's full open (which refused past 2 GiB — the incident's broken rescue) is replaced by proceeding with the tail-anchored windowed session. Trajectory `view/cost/inspect` materialize the branch via the new `SessionTree.ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → `WindowedSessionStorage.loadAllOlder()` (sequential bounded-block forward scan, no full-open refusal); `tail` polls stay windowed. ### Key decisions - `loadAllOlder()` (sequential strips from file head, one splice) chosen over reusing `growOlderUntil` — the boundary-walk's doubling strips + per-strip record cap amplified read/parse ~13× over a whole file (30k-record bench: 9.6s vs 0.85s full open). - `_indexChunk` now block-prepends (`insertAll`) instead of per-record `insert(0)` — suspended-eviction walks had made it O(n²). - Subagent registry source no longer hard-casts `_repo as JsonlSessionRepo`; foreign repos degrade to an empty registry instead of crashing. - Degradation contract preserved (F3 NEG): a genuinely corrupt session still reports inline through the picker catch; only the refusal-producing full open is gone. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart test/session/session_tree_test.dart dart test test/cli/sessions_picker_test.dart test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart ``` Regression runs: `test/session` (314), `test/trajectory` (197), `test/agent`+`test/hub` (548), `test/cli` (3529) all green; trajectory perf gate within budget (97 MB real CLI path, parse 791 ms / total 5.4 s). `dart analyze` clean on all touched files. ### Not in this slice (follow-ups) AC3a streaming trajectory export (exporters still snapshot-based), W2 rotation activation, W3 write-side caps (owner-call, opt-in), picker "too large to preview" badge UI, E2E/nightly oversize fixtures (AC8). Known pre-existing, reproduced on unmodified main: `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` aborts the VM at teardown (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk`) and kills whole-directory `dart test` runs that include it — run it in isolation.
