# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
2066 AGENTS.md

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
2066 AGENTS.md

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # Issue #1234 rework: 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override (a

      # 019ede65), and the package config's sources drive the CRAP census
      # too, so test/ + example/ get the SAME loc gate from the companion
      # config (crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml) — the scope the retired shell
      # guards (gh-1232) scanned there. No baseline: nothing exceeds 2800
      # today, and the ceiling itself is the point.
      - name: Loc scope gate (test/ + example/, gh-1232 whole-tree ceiling)

          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens

          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # config (crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml) — the scope the retired shell
      # guards (gh-1232) scanned there. No baseline: nothing exceeds 2800
      # today, and the ceiling itself is the point.
      - name: Loc scope gate (test/ + example/, gh-1232 whole-tree ceiling)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc

arguments.content:
Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.

Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.

Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`.

Extracted the single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` — three parallel `insertAll(0, …)` calls (one memmove per list) plus the per-record re-index (`_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache`), with a doc noting the window-list invariant it guards and its two callers. `_indexChunk`'s `prepend` branch now builds the three parallel lists and delegates; `_spliceOlderAbove` was removed and `loadAllOlder` calls `_blockPrepend` directly (a one-line delegate would have been needless indirection). The O(n²)→block-prepend history is preserved in `_blockPrepend`'s doc.

Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_4.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_4.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_4.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.
2. **The exact regression shape** — whole-ledger prime, then a *fresh windowed re-open per poll* (the shipped bug's composition): the poll window returns only the resident tail, shorter than the primed ledger; the id-based `TrajectoryTailer` still renders the appended record (`late!`). This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.

{"content":"Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.

{"content":"Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

{"content":"Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.
